# Have a good day

The Core Responsibilities protocol: *what needs to happen for me to feel good
about today?* Ends with what was actually there: no score, no streak, no
percentage.

⚠️ **Not a full conversion.** Version 1 of this module offered three tick
lists (`needs`, `enjoy`, `soothe`) drawn live from a separate "Map" module's
own fields, and a `didlog` that ticked off which of those picks actually
happened. Version 2 has no question kind yet for "options pulled from
another activity's list" or "tick what you picked earlier" — see `SPEC.md`
§13. Until one exists, this file keeps only the free-text question and the
plain follow-up questions; the map-linked lists and the tick-off are dropped
rather than faked.

## Adding it to a booklet

Open this file on its own, or copy everything below the front matter into
your own booklet, above the long rule.

> [!module|mensio-the-day] Have a good day

What needs to happen today.

> [!activity|day repeat] Have a good day

Not the to-do list, and not a target. The question is what has to be there for you to get to the end of today and feel you carried your weight — which is usually shorter and more specific than everything you could do.

> [!text|extra long] Anything else that would make today satisfying
> In your own words.

> [!text|mind] On my mind today
> What keeps coming back, in a sentence or two.

> [!text|exploring] What I'm exploring or trying
> Something in motion, however small.

> [!text|aside] What I'm setting aside for today
> A worry or task that can wait. Naming it here is not the same as dismissing it.

> [!text|help] What would help today
> A person, a condition, a resource, a smaller scope.

> [!text|carry] One thing to carry forward
> From yesterday, or from the last entry.

> [!module|mensio-the-day end] End of Have a good day
